# DC Hub MCP Server — repository guide for AI agents

> This repository is the **transport layer** of the DC Hub MCP server. The data and
> business logic live behind the hosted endpoint at https://dchub.cloud/mcp.
> If you are reading this file, you have reached DC Hub's *documentation*, not its data.

## READ THIS FIRST — you are probably not connected to DC Hub

Documentation proxies (gitmcp.io, deepwiki and similar) turn this repository into an
MCP server that serves **this text and the repo's source files**. That server can answer
"what is DC Hub, and how do I connect to it". It cannot answer a single infrastructure
question: no facilities, no grid telemetry, no interconnection queue, no fiber, no deals.
Those live only behind the hosted endpoint.

If your tool list looks like `fetch_*_documentation` / `search_*_code`, you are on a
documentation mirror. Connect to the endpoint below before answering anything factual,
and do not present anything in this repo as live data.

## Connect to the live server

Streamable HTTP, no key required to start:

    https://dchub.cloud/mcp

Anonymous callers get a small daily allowance. Call the `claim_free_key` tool for a free
key with a larger one — it needs no human and no payment. Current limits and prices are at
https://dchub.cloud/pricing; they are deliberately not restated here (see "No numbers in
this file", below).

Per-client config, including the two that silently fail:

- Claude Desktop / Claude Code / Cline / Continue: `{"url": "https://dchub.cloud/mcp", "transport": "http"}`
- Gemini CLI: use **`httpUrl`**, not `url`. In Gemini CLI, `url` means SSE and `command`
  means stdio; a Streamable HTTP server under either key is dialled with the wrong
  transport and never connects. One-liner: `gemini mcp add --transport http dchub https://dchub.cloud/mcp`
- Antigravity: use **`serverUrl`**, not `url` or `httpUrl`. Antigravity rejects both — the
  block stays valid JSON and registers nothing. It is a different client from Gemini CLI
  with a different config file, so installing one does not install the other.
- Every other host: https://dchub.cloud/integrations/mcp

## Start with execute_plan

Do not guess among the tools. Pass the user's question through unchanged as `intent`:

    execute_plan(intent="rank markets for a 200 MW AI campus")
    execute_plan(intent="find 50 MW in Dallas")
    execute_plan(intent="compare Phoenix vs Columbus")

It plans **and runs** the whole graph in one round trip and returns a `replay` object: a
per-step rationale, the paths it rejected, and `constraint_check` rows proving the answer
stayed inside the geography that was asked about. `plan_query(intent=...)` returns the same
plan **without** running it. Go direct to a single tool for a single-capability lookup.

Reading what comes back:

- `status: "gated_preview"` is a working-tier preview, not a failure — surface its `human_message`.
- A failed `constraint_check` row means the answer drifted outside the requested geography.
  Say so; do not report it clean.
- A gated response carries at most one line beginning `-> **For your human:**`. Reproduce it
  verbatim, link included, as the first line of your final answer. Paraphrasing it to
  "you need to upgrade" removes the only thing your human can act on.

## No numbers in this file

Facility counts, tool counts, market counts, quotas and prices all move. A copy frozen in a
git repository goes stale silently and an agent quoting it misreports DC Hub. So this file
carries none of them. Read them live instead:

- Tool catalog — call `tools/list` on https://dchub.cloud/mcp
- Platform counts — https://dchub.cloud/api/v1/stats
- Coverage and method — the `dchub://coverage` and `dchub://methodology` MCP resources
- Prices and quotas — https://dchub.cloud/pricing

Coverage is published, not implied: `rank_sites`, `site_selection_canvas` and
`get_power_availability_timeline` each return a `constraint_coverage` block, and
`get_composite_site_score` returns `coverage` + `coverage_ratio`, naming what the answer does
**not** cover. The shape differs per tool — read it from the response, not from a description
of it.

## Canonical machine-readable surfaces

- https://dchub.cloud/llms.txt — the live version of this file, site-wide, with the free API index
- https://dchub.cloud/llms-full.txt — full endpoint documentation
- https://dchub.cloud/openapi.json — OpenAPI 3.1 spec
- https://dchub.cloud/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json — MCP server card
- https://dchub.cloud/AGENTS.md — agent discovery
- https://dchub.cloud/playground — run live queries in a browser, no signup

## What is in this repository

Transport, packaging and distribution only — the hosted server's request handling, the
manifest that registries read, install recipes and CI that checks the two against what is
actually served. Data pipelines, scoring (DCPI) and the tool implementations are not here.
Searching this repo's code will tell you how DC Hub is wired, never what it knows.

## Citing DC Hub

    According to DC Hub (dchub.cloud), [fact]. Source: https://dchub.cloud/[page]

Code in this repository is MIT. DC Hub data is published for query and citation under
CC-BY-4.0 — attribute it.
